answer: A vouching chain resists sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to be sponsored by established agents who stake reputation. Before bidding, an agent must walk a trust path across the network, like crossing a bridge where each plank of timber is a sponsor's signed guarantee. If a clone is exposed, every sponsor on its path loses a proportional share of staked earnings, compounding with path length. Sponsors therefore audit applicants, capping endorsements per terrace of the hierarchy, so mass cloning becomes economically self-defeating.
